newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises peak power prices for Monday slightly.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises peak power prices for Monday slightly.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised prices for power during peak demand hours on Monday by $1.00 to $3.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said Friday.
BPA also offered displacement power for a block running from 0100 PST Saturday to 0600 PST Monday at $6.00 per MWh.

BPA offered up to 500 MW of firm, peak power for Monday at $12.00 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $13.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales, up from $11.00 and $12.00, respectively, for Friday.
Monday firm off-peak prices were unchanged at $10.50 per MWh for all deliveries.
Up to 500 MW of non-firm power for hours ending 0800-1000 and 1800-2000 PST on Monday was offered at $15.00 (Northwest) and $16.00 (COB), up from $12.00 and $13.00, respectively, for Friday.
Non-firm power during shoulder hours (1100-1700 and 2100-2200) was offered at $11.25 (Northwest) and $12.50 (COB), barely changed from Friday.
Non-firm power during off-peak hours on Monday was offered at $10.75 for all deliveries, up slightly from $10.50.
BPA's prices for Saturday and Sunday were nearly flat with Friday prices.
